newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Increases in fuel, inflation and in the public debt will be the result of the increasingly stronger dollar, pound and yen. The rise of the dollar against the drachma yesterday by 5.2 drachmas will have no long-term effects on the Greek economy but if the rate of increase is maintained - the dollar has appreciated by 14.2 percent since the beginning of the year - it will become a source of inflationary pressure and increase drachma spending on fuel and dollar-pegged imports.

--The course towards economic and monetary union (EMU) and the Greeke conomy will come under the microscope today at a meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Costas Simitis with National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou and Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos.
--The dollar and pound surged against the drachma yesterday while bankers believe the yen still has the margins to reach 250 drahmas.
--Consumer loans on credit cards totalled a massive 572 billion drachmas in 1996, a 400 percent increase in the 1990-1996 period, according to an ICAP study.
--Papandoniou will meet with his deputy ministers to confer on measures to turn around the flagging fortunes of public revenues in the first half-year.

--The National Tourist Organisation of Greece, EOT, is undertaking marathon efforts to save the funds allocated to tourist projects under the Second Community Support Framework business programme and not committed as yet. According to reports, Deputy National Economy Minister Christos Pachtas will chair a meeting on heads of CSF programmes to discuss progress or lack thereof.

--The results of today's bond auction is awaited with interest, given the negative climate created by the upward trend in interbank interest rates and a significant fall in prices of bonds on the secondary market.

--The volume of retail sales increased by 2.5 percent in April while turnover increased 1.5 percent. A meeting yesterday at the development ministry expressed the opinion that the prices of fresh produce would gradually fall by end-August and that prices of basic goods at supermarkets were slightly reduced, with subsequent positive effects on the inflation rate.
--The finance ministry's refusal to act on nominal price lists has put obstacles in the way of at least two leasing firms planning listing on the stock exchange.

--The European Commission will decide on the fate of the Skaramangas Shipyards tomorrow, although sources say the outcome will be positive. The writing off of the shipyard's debts and an investment programme of 15.625 billion drachmas will be discussed at the meeting tomorrow. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
